title: Robot vacuum features explained: An easy buying guide from a professional reviewer
excerpt: I give robot vacuum advice to friends and family all the time. Here's my checklist.
content_html:

Recommendations for the best robot vacuums to buy in 2026 are at the bottom of this guide. Use the table of contents to skip down to that, or to skip to the deep dive on a specific robot vacuum feature.

Deciding between a robot vacuum and a stick vacuum ultimately comes down to one factor: which one you'll actually use on a regular basis. If you're struggling to keep a manual vacuuming routine, let this be your sign to finally switch to the automated version. A good robot vacuum can completely change the way you keep up with your home. You just have to know what to look for.

What to know before buying a robot vacuum

The holy trinity of non-negotiable robot vacuum features — automatic emptying, mopping, and smart mapping — can be found at any price point these days. Despite the less intimidating cost spectrum, it's still possible to underpay or overpay for a robot vacuum. The question isn't whether or not a robot vacuum is worth it in your home at all. It's about which robot vacuum features will give each household the best automated cleaning experience.

You May Also Like

I have a pretty good sense of that: I've been testing robot vacuums for Mashable since 2019. More than 40 different robot vacuums have lived under my roof so far, and my running mental checklist for robot vacuum shopping gets refreshed on a monthly basis. I can barely attend a family function without being asked for robot vacuum advice, anyway, so I've organized my firsthand intel into a robot vacuum buying guide for the internet. Here's your straightforward robot vacuum buying guide for 2026:

Robot vacuum suction power explained

Technical translation: Most robot vacuum brands measure suction power in pascals (Pa). iRobot and Shark are the two outliers. They tend to advertise a certain vacuum's suction power by comparing it to another model from their own lineup.

As of 2026, the most powerful robot vacuums you can buy have between 35,000 and 36,000 Pa of suction power. You'll want to aim for the highest suction power possible in homes with plush carpet or lots of area rugs and more than two pets. Anything hitting 20,000 Pa or above would still be considered good suction power for a robot vacuum in homes with slightly less intense cleaning needs, less foot traffic, or less fur.

The path clearly shows where this Roborock's 36,000 Pa suction has been. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

This Dreame vacuum has dual brush rolls made of two different textures. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

Pro tip: If you're looking for a robot vacuum that works well on carpet, the brush roll setup underneath also matters. In my experience, the best robot vacuum pet hair pickup comes from a dual brush roll system where the rollers sit parallel to each other. They spin independently of each other to pinch hair in the middle (and give clumps an exit to prevent tangling or spooling at the end of the roll).

The most effective rollers use alternating materials like hairbrush-like bristles, nylon bristles, and rubber fins for digging deep in carpet fibers, creating friction and agitation on stubborn shedding, and latching onto thick and fine hair.

Some robot vacuums also have a dedicated extendable edge sweeping brush, which has more purpose in life than the aimless side brushes affixed to most cheap robot vacuums. The retractable arm reaches an inch or two past the robot's body to push debris out from tight spots into the vacuum's cleaning path — picture crumbs under the counter or dust bunnies blown near walls.

What to avoid: I would generally advise against settling for suction power below 10,000 Pa; though 8,000 Pa or below is where I draw a hard line for any household. The weaker the suction power, the higher the chances of debris being scattered instead of sucked or pet hair being left behind — two experiences that'll quickly make you regret spending money on this robot vacuum.

Self-emptying docks explained

Technical translation: A self-emptying robot vacuum automatically empties its debris into the same dock it charges on. The dust bin in the dock has a much larger capacity than the dust bin on the vacuum itself. Instead of dumping that tiny dustbin by hand multiple times per week, automatic emptying gets you off the hook from dustbin maintenance for at least a month, if not much longer.

Just about every robot vacuum is a self-emptying robot vacuum these days, even at the ultra-budget-friendly level. Unless you need the vacuum to live under a TV stand or a couch, there's no need to spend time pondering whether automatic emptying is worth it. There's no shortage of compact self-emptying robot vacuums that would be great for a small space like an apartment.

The Dreame D20 Pro Plus self-empty dock is on the small side. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

The Dreame X60 Max Ultra Complete dock is more advanced, but takes up more space. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

Pretty much all robot vacuums are mopping robot vacuums at this point in the game. That's the case even at the $200 to $300 end of the spectrum. However, the best robot vacuum and mop combos have a much more advanced strategy and scrubbing intensity than entry-level mopping robot vacuums. There are three main mopping pad designs to choose from:

Regular flat mopping pad: Most cheap robot vacuum mop combos use a basic D-shaped pad. This design typically doesn't vibrate, press down onto the floor, or reach along edges, so this type of wet cleaning maxes out at wiping up small droplets, fine dust, or pet hair on hard floors. Don't expect a stationary flat mopping pad to soak up larger spills or anything with a chunky or sticky consistency — that's when smearing happens.

The budget-friendly Dreame D20 Pro Plus. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

The Shark UV Reveal's flat pad pops in and out during spot cleaning. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

The Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal 2-in-1 and the Roborock Saros 20 Sonic are two exceptions. Both are equipped with a D-shaped mopping pad that scrubs with pressurized sonic vibrations and scoots out when corners or walls are sensed.

Dual spinning mopping pads: This common design divvies the job up to two circular pads that spin to create more physical agitation on dried stains, offering more elbow grease than a singular stationary pad. Dual spinning mopping pads are the optimal design for edge mopping because their scrubbing isn't limited to the vacuum's round shape. One circular pad operates on a hinge that swings out when a wall or corner is sensed.

Mashable Trend Report

This Roborock was able to mop under the fridge and reach the crumbs lodged at the edge. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

Dreame's spinning pads were highly effective on dried winter slush and salty shoe prints near the door. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

Roller mop: Roller mop robot vacuums use a paint roller-style pad that spans the diameter of the vacuum. The rollers are typically thick and fluffy with an absorbent bath towel-like material, making this design elite for soaking up liquids. Roller mop robot vacuums have the unique ability to rinse their pad with fresh water during mopping, so they're the least likely type to streak your clean floors with dirty water.

The Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

Previously, only spinning mopping pads had cleaned this closely in my bathroom doorway. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

Self-cleaning mopping pads

You're buying a robot vacuum because you don't feel like doing your own vacuuming and mopping, right? If a shorter to-do list is the goal, I doubt you'll feel like refilling a tiny water tank or touching soggy mopping pads every day. You can get out of this by choosing a robot vacuum and mop that can wash and dry its own mopping pads. This is an option for a ton of models with spinning pads or a roller mop.

Their self-empty dock also houses two water tanks — one for rinsing and refilling clean water, and one to hold the dirty water — plus fans beneath the vacuum for drying. Almost all of them dry with hot air to kill bacteria and mitigate that mildewy smell. The clean water tank in the dock can last for a week or so before needing a refill, which is around the same time that the dirty water tank will need to be emptied.

The water tanks can be filled and emptied in the sink. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

Self-refilling docks have a special detergent dispensing compartment. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

For enhanced sanitation, many high-end robot vacuums can mop with a cleaning solution rather than just plain water. Brands often throw a bottle of their official cleaning solution in the box, but the fine print should let you know if it's safe to branch out to other detergents with your preferred ingredients or scent.

Pro tip: Some models also use heated water while they're actually mopping. Heated mopping loosens the bonds that make grease slimy and hard to wipe up. These are the only robot vacuum mop combos I've tested that can successfully clean up oily dressings or syrup without leaving a trail of sticky residue.

What to avoid: Robot vacuums that don't mop aren't worth it, even if you don't think you'll use the mopping part. Most non-mopping robot vacuums are basic on all fronts: They have weak suction, aren't great at navigating, and require you to empty the dustbin by hand.

iRobot has a pretty powerful Roomba that doesn't mop, but at $699.99, you're not exactly saving money by forgoing mopping. There are far better robot vacuum mop combos out there that cost the same or less. If you don't feel like dealing with mopping-related maintenance, just ignore the mopping part altogether and take advantage of that vacuum's other solid features.

Robot vacuum smart mapping explained

Technical translation: Smart mapping refers to a robot vacuum's ability to scope out and remember a copy of your home's floor plan. The map drawn during the vacuum's initial mapping run pops up in the app, where you tweak it by merging or splitting rooms and adding room labels. Then, the robot vacuum can clean specific rooms on command, or complete a whole-home clean.

A map of my apartment in the Roborock app. Credit: Screenshot / Roborock

A close-up of my living room's furniture arrangement in the Eufy app. Credit: Screenshot / Eufy

LiDAR measures the distance between boundaries and large objects in the room by bouncing lasers off of walls and furniture to see how fast the light comes back. (This is what the circular tower atop many robot vacuums is for.) LiDAR works instantaneously, so map-making is quick and highly accurate even in large homes. LiDAR robot vacuums don't require light to see, so they work just as well at night or in dark rooms.

VSLAM uses cameras that continuously capture images of the space and identify room-specific landmarks like the layout of a wall, a doorway, or a large piece of furniture. VSLAM is meticulous when assessing objects up close, but it's not as equipped for open floor plans as LiDAR is. VSLAM cameras can't see as well in low lighting, either.

In 2026, many flagship robot vacuums mesh the two approaches to achieve seamless navigation in any situation it stumbles across. The combination of the two is ideal for floor type detection. Premium robot vacuums can sense hard floors, rugs, and fully carpeted rooms, labeling them that way in the app. Most have an automatic suction boost feature that kicks in on soft floors.

Zone cleaning and keep-out zones

Room-by-room smart mapping also allows robot vacuums to clean specific areas in those rooms. In the app, you can drag and drop a zone to clean up a spill or deal with crumbs near the table without cleaning the entire room. These can be a one-time thing or saved as a recurring command in the future. Similarly, zones can also be used to keep the vacuum out of certain spots, like around a pile of Legos or a frilly bath mat.

What to avoid: I'll die on the hill that smart mapping is the baseline brain power that any robot vacuum worth your money should have. The bump-and-go approach provides too many opportunities for a robot vacuum to get stuck, potentially making your life harder instead of easier. If you think about it, actual cleaning skills don't even come into play if a robot vacuum can't successfully get itself to the spots that need to be cleaned.

Luckily, smart mapping isn't a tall order nowadays — brands rarely release a new robot vacuum without it. A budget cap of $200 is more than enough to secure room-to-room mapping from reliable brands like Shark or Roborock. To be sure, scan the product listing to make sure that "LiDAR" or "map" is specifically mentioned. Older Roombas used sneaky language like "smart navigation methodically cleans in neat rows," which is not smart mapping.

Small obstacle avoidance explained

Technical translation: Small obstacle avoidance technology helps a robot vacuum dodge low-profile objects in real time. This special camera system can detect obstacles like shoes, laundry, chargers and extension cords, pet toys, or other items that commonly pop up on the floor. With obstacle avoidance, you won't have to worry about pre-tidying the floor before sending the vacuum out.

Many obstacle avoidance cameras can even decipher between several different types of objects. You'll see a bubble on the map marking where the item was found. It's always nice to have proof that your vacuum is, in fact, avoiding problem areas (even if you didn't set a keep-out zone).

Livestream pet cameras

The cameras used for small obstacle avoidance aren't necessarily the kind that take pictures. But some fancier robot vacuums actually can snap photos and capture a livestream video. These give you a floor-level view of whatever the vacuum sees as it's roving your home, making it a pretty comforting tool for pet parents when they're away. Most livestream pet cameras are even accompanied by two-way microphones to talk to your pets or call another person who's at home.

Pro tip: If this sketches you out, you don't have to enable usage of the camera at all. If livestream remote viewing is activated by someone in the app, the robot makes an announcement to make sure anyone at home is aware.

AI mess detection

It's becoming the norm for small obstacle avoidance cameras to use AI to become better drivers and better cleaners over time. Several flagship robot vacuums from 2026 can assess different types of messes on the floor to adjust cleaning intensity accordingly. The smartest ones can tell the difference between a few everyday crumbs and a big pile of dry debris, or mop the site of a big liquid spill twice.

What I see when the Narwal Flow 2 is cleaning near the litter box... Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

... vs. what the Narwal Flow 2 sees: scattered debris and my cat, Sansa. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

Pro tip: If you're not big on AI, you can turn off AI features without completely disabling small obstacle avoidance.

What is good battery life for a robot vacuum?

It depends on how big your space is. A 90- to 100-minute battery life is sufficient for a robot vacuum to cover an apartment or single story of a small home on one charge. Many newer robot vacuums can last up to 250 minutes on one charge, which would be ideal for a full clean of a house that's several thousand square feet. But battery life shouldn't be a huge deciding factor if most of your cleaning will be done on a room-by-room basis, anyway.

Pro tip: Every robot vacuum you'll find at a retailer like Amazon or Target is a self-charging robot vacuum. Unless you're investing in a 15-year-old vacuum you found on eBay, even the cheapest robot vacuums know to return to the dock when their battery is low. The cleaning session should resume once they're juiced up.

本指南的底部提供了 2026 年最佳购买机器人吸尘器的建议。 使用目录跳至该内容，或跳至深入了解特定的机器人吸尘器功能。

在机器人真空吸尘器和棒式真空吸尘器之间做出决定最终取决于一个因素：您实际上会定期使用哪一个。 如果您正在努力保持手动吸尘程序，请让这成为您最终切换到自动版本的标志。 一台好的扫地机器人可以彻底改变您打扫家居的方式。 您只需要知道要寻找什么即可。

购买扫地机器人之前需要了解什么

如今，机器人真空吸尘器的三大无可争议的功能——自动清空、拖地和智能地图——在任何价位都可以找到。 尽管成本范围不那么吓人，但仍然有可能为机器人真空吸尘器支付少付或多付的费用。 问题不在于机器人吸尘器是否值得在家中使用。 这是关于机器人吸尘器的哪些功能将为每个家庭带来最佳的自动清洁体验。

你可能也喜欢

我对此有一个很好的认识：自 2019 年以来，我一直在测试 Mashable 的扫地机器人。 到目前为止，我家已经拥有超过 40 种不同的扫地机器人，我的扫地机器人购物清单每月都会刷新。 无论如何，我几乎无法参加家庭活动而不被要求提供机器人真空吸尘器的建议，所以我将我的第一手资料整理成互联网机器人真空吸尘器购买指南。 这是 2026 年简单的扫地机器人购买指南：

机器人真空吸力解释

技术翻译：大多数扫地机器人品牌都以帕斯卡 (Pa) 为单位测量吸力。 iRobot 和 Shark 是两个异常值。 他们倾向于通过将某种真空吸尘器与自己产品系列中的其他型号进行比较来宣传其吸力。

截至 2026 年，您可以买到的最强大的机器人真空吸尘器的吸力在 35,000 至 36,000 Pa 之间。 在有毛绒地毯或大量小地毯和两只以上宠物的家庭中，您需要尽可能获得最高的吸力。 对于清洁需求稍低、人流量较少或皮毛较少的家庭中的机器人吸尘器来说，任何达到 20,000 Pa 或以上的吸力仍然被认为是良好的吸力。

该路径清楚地显示了石头扫地机器人 36,000 Pa 吸力的所在位置。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

这款 Dreame 吸尘器具有由两种不同纹理制成的双刷辊。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

专业提示：如果您正在寻找一款在地毯上运行良好的机器人真空吸尘器，那么下面的刷辊设置也很重要。 根据我的经验，最好的机器人真空宠物毛发拾取器来自双刷辊系统，其中辊彼此平行。 它们彼此独立旋转，将头发夹在中间（并为发束提供出口，以防止在卷末端缠结或缠绕）。

最有效的滚筒使用交替材料，如发刷状刷毛、尼龙刷毛和橡胶翅片，深入地毯纤维，在顽固脱落时产生摩擦和搅动，并粘住浓密和细小的毛发。

一些机器人真空吸尘器还配有专用的可伸缩边缘清扫刷，与大多数廉价机器人真空吸尘器上固定的漫无目的的侧刷相比，它在生活中具有更多用途。 可伸缩的手臂伸到机器人身体上方一两英寸处，将碎片从狭窄的地方推入真空吸尘器的清洁路径——柜台下的图片碎屑或墙壁附近吹起的灰尘。

应避免的事项：我通常建议不要将吸力设置为低于 10,000 Pa；不过 8,000 Pa 或以下是我对任何家庭划定的强硬界限。 吸力越弱，碎片被散落而不是被吸走或宠物毛发被留下的机会就越大——这两种经历很快就会让你后悔在这款机器人真空吸尘器上花钱。

自动清空码头解释

技术翻译：自清空机器人真空吸尘器会自动将其碎片倒入其充电的同一个底座中。 扩展坞中的垃圾箱的容量比真空吸尘器本身的垃圾箱大得多。 自动清空功能无需每周多次手动倾倒那个小垃圾箱，而是可以让您在至少一个月（甚至更长时间）内摆脱垃圾箱维护的麻烦。

如今，几乎每个机器人真空吸尘器都是自动清空机器人真空吸尘器，即使是在超预算友好的水平上。 除非您需要将真空吸尘器放在电视柜或沙发下，否则无需花时间思考自动清空是否值得。 市面上不乏紧凑型自动清空机器人吸尘器，非常适合公寓等狭小的空间。

Dreame D20 Pro Plus 自空坞站尺寸偏小。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

Dreame X60 Max Ultra Complete 底座更先进，但占用更多空间。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

在游戏的此时，几乎所有机器人真空吸尘器都在拖地机器人真空吸尘器。 即使在 200 至 300 美元的范围内也是如此。 然而，最好的扫地机器人和拖把组合比入门级扫地机器人具有更先进的策略和擦洗强度。 拖布垫主要有以下三种设计可供选择：

普通扁平拖地垫：大多数便宜的机器人真空拖把组合使用基本的 D 形拖地垫。 这种设计通常不会振动，不会压到地板上，也不会沿着边缘延伸，因此这种类型的湿式清洁可以最大程度地擦拭硬地板上的小水滴、细小灰尘或宠物毛发。 不要指望固定的扁平拖把垫能够吸收较大的溢出物或任何具有厚实或粘稠稠度的东西 - 这时候就会发生涂抹。

经济实惠的 Dreame D20 Pro Plus。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

Shark UV Reveal 的平垫在局部清洁期间会弹出和弹出。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal 二合一和 Roborock Saros 20 Sonic 是两个例外。 两者都配备了 D 形拖把垫，可通过加压声波振动进行擦洗，并在感应到角落或墙壁时迅速伸出。

双旋转拖把垫：这种常见的设计将工作分配给两个圆形垫，它们旋转以对干燥的污渍产生更多的物理搅拌，比单个固定垫提供更多的肘部油脂。 双旋转拖把垫是边缘拖地的最佳设计，因为它们的擦洗不限于真空吸尘器的圆形形状。 一个圆形垫在铰链上运行，当检测到墙壁或角落时，铰链就会向外摆动。

可混搭趋势报告

这款 Roborock 能够拖地冰箱下方并触及边缘的面包屑。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

Dreame 的旋转垫对于干燥的冬季雪泥和门附近的咸味鞋印非常有效。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

滚筒拖把：滚筒拖把机器人真空吸尘器使用跨越真空吸尘器直径的油漆滚筒式垫。 滚筒通常又厚又蓬松，采用类似浴巾的吸收性材料，使这种设计成为吸收液体的精英。 滚轮拖把机器人真空吸尘器具有独特的能力，可以在拖地过程中用清水冲洗其垫子，因此它们是最不可能用脏水在干净的地板上留下痕迹的类型。

Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

以前，只有旋转拖把才能清洁我浴室门口的地方。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

自清洁拖地垫

您购买扫地机器人是因为您不想自己吸尘和拖地，对吗？ 如果目标是缩短待办事项清单，我怀疑您会想每天给小水箱加水或触摸湿漉漉的拖把垫。 您可以通过选择可以清洗和干燥自己的拖布垫的机器人吸尘器和拖把来摆脱这个问题。 这是许多带有旋转垫或滚筒拖把的型号的一个选项。

他们的自清码头还装有两个水箱——一个用于冲洗和补充干净的水，另一个用于容纳脏水——以及真空吸尘器下方用于干燥的风扇。 几乎所有的东西都用热空气干燥，以杀死细菌并减轻霉味。 码头中的净水箱可以持续一周左右，然后需要重新加水，这大约与脏水箱需要清空的时间相同。

水箱可以在水槽中注水和清空。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

自动补充底座有一个特殊的清洁剂分配室。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

为了加强卫生，许多高端机器人真空吸尘器可以使用清洁溶液而不是普通水来拖地。 品牌经常在盒子里放一瓶官方清洁剂，但细则应该会让你知道是否可以安全地使用其他含有你喜欢的成分或气味的清洁剂。

专业提示：有些型号在实际拖地时也会使用热水。 加热拖把会松开使油脂变得粘稠且难以擦掉的粘合物。 这是我测试过的唯一可以成功清理油性敷料或糖浆而不留下粘性残留物的机器人真空拖把组合。

应避免的事项：即使您认为自己不会使用拖地部分，不拖地的扫地机器人也不值得购买。 大多数非拖地机器人真空吸尘器在各方面都很基础：它们的吸力较弱，不擅长导航，并且需要您手动清空垃圾箱。

iRobot 有一款非常强大的 Roomba，不拖地，但售价 699.99 美元，你并不能通过放弃拖地来省钱。 有更好的机器人真空拖把组合，价格相同或更低。 如果您不想处理与拖地相关的维护，只需完全忽略拖地部分并利用真空吸尘器的其他可靠功能即可。

机器人真空智能测绘解释

技术翻译：智能地图是指机器人吸尘器能够确定并记住您家的平面图副本的能力。 在真空吸尘器初始映射运行期间绘制的地图会在应用程序中弹出，您可以在其中通过合并或分割房间以及添加房间标签来调整它。 然后，机器人吸尘器可以根据命令清洁特定房间，或完成整个家庭的清洁。

Roborock 应用程序中我公寓的地图。 图片来源：截图/Roborock

Eufy 应用程序中我客厅家具布置的特写。 图片来源：截图/Eufy

激光雷达通过从墙壁和家具上反射激光来测量光线返回的速度，从而测量边界与房间内大型物体之间的距离。 （这就是许多机器人吸尘器顶部圆形塔的用途。） 激光雷达可即时工作，因此即使在大型住宅中，地图制作也能快速且高度准确。 激光雷达扫地机器人不需要光线就能看到，因此它们在夜间或黑暗的房间里也能正常工作。

VSLAM 使用摄像头连续捕捉空间图像并识别房间特定的地标，例如墙壁、门口或大型家具的布局。 VSLAM 在近距离评估物体时非常细致，但它不像 LiDAR 那样适合开放式平面图。 VSLAM 相机在低光照条件下的视野也不佳。

到 2026 年，许多旗舰机器人真空吸尘器将这两种方法结合起来，在遇到的任何情况下实现无缝导航。 两者的结合非常适合地板类型检测。 高级扫地机器人可以感知硬地板、地毯和铺满地毯的房间，并在应用程序中对它们进行标记。 大多数都具有自动吸力增强功能，可在柔软的地板上发挥作用。

区域清洁和禁止区域

逐个房间的智能地图还允许机器人吸尘器清洁这些房间的特定区域。 在应用程序中，您可以拖放一个区域来清理溢出物或处理桌子附近的面包屑，而无需清洁整个房间。 这些可以是一次性的事情，也可以保存为将来的重复命令。 同样，区域也可用于防止某些地方出现真空，例如一堆乐高积木或褶边浴室防滑垫周围。

要避免什么：我会死在山上，智能地图是任何值得你花钱的机器人真空吸尘器应该拥有的基线脑力。 这种碰碰即走的方法为扫地机器人提供了太多被卡住的机会，这可能会让您的生活变得更加困难而不是更轻松。 如果您想一想，如果扫地机器人无法成功到达需要清洁的地方，那么实际的清洁技能甚至无法发挥作用。

幸运的是，如今智能地图并不是一项艰巨的任务——品牌很少发布没有它的新型扫地机器人。 200 美元的预算上限足以确保 Shark 或 Roborock 等可靠品牌提供房间到房间的地图绘制。 为确保安全，请扫描产品列表以确保特别提到“LiDAR”或“地图”。 较旧的 Roombas 使用了一些偷偷摸摸的语言，例如“智能导航有条不紊地清理整齐的行”，这不是智能映射。

小障碍物回避解释

技术翻译：小型避障技术帮助机器人真空实时躲避低矮物体。 这种特殊的摄像头系统可以检测鞋子、衣物、充电器和延长线、宠物玩具或其他通常出现在地板上的物品等障碍物。 通过避障，您无需担心在送出吸尘器之前预先清理地板。

许多避障摄像机甚至可以区分几种不同类型的物体。 您会在地图上看到一个气泡，标记了找到该物品的位置。 能够证明您的真空吸尘器实际上避开了问题区域（即使您没有设置禁区）总是一件好事。

直播宠物摄像机

用于小型避障的摄像头不一定是拍照的摄像头。 但一些更高级的机器人吸尘器实际上可以拍照并捕捉直播视频。 这些让您可以在地板上看到吸尘器在您家里巡游时所看到的一切，这对于宠物父母外出时来说是一个非常舒适的工具。 大多数直播宠物摄像机甚至都配有双向麦克风，可以与您的宠物交谈或呼叫家里的其他人。

专业提示：如果这对您有所帮助，那么您根本不必启用相机。 如果应用程序中的某人激活了直播远程查看，机器人会发出公告以确保家里的任何人都知道。

AI混乱检测

随着时间的推移，小型避障摄像头使用人工智能来成为更好的驾驶员和更好的清洁工正在成为常态。 2026 年的几款旗舰机器人真空吸尘器可以评估地板上不同类型的脏乱情况，从而相应地调整清洁强度。 最聪明的人可以区分一些日常碎屑和一大堆干燥的碎片，或者用拖把拖两次大量液体溢出的地方。

... 对比 Narwal Flow 2 所看到的：散落的碎片和我的猫 Sansa。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

专业提示：如果您对人工智能不感兴趣，您可以关闭人工智能功能，而无需完全禁用小障碍物回避。

扫地机器人的电池寿命有多长？

这取决于你的空间有多大。 机器人吸尘器的电池续航时间为 90 至 100 分钟，一次充电足以覆盖一间公寓或单层小住宅。 许多新型扫地机器人一次充电可持续使用长达 250 分钟，这对于全面清洁数千平方英尺的房屋来说是理想的选择。 但无论如何，如果你的大部分清洁工作是逐个房间进行的，那么电池寿命就不应该成为一个重要的决定因素。

专业提示：您在亚马逊或塔吉特等零售商处找到的每台机器人真空吸尘器都是自动充电机器人真空吸尘器。 除非您投资的是在 eBay 上找到的已使用 15 年的吸尘器，否则即使是最便宜的扫地机器人也会在电池电量不足时返回底座。 一旦它们被榨汁，清洁工作就应该恢复。
